item.title: NOTICE OF RATIFICATION OF A MINOR RULES VIOLATION
item.description:
Citywide Administrative Services | Special Materials | Notice In plain English (machine-written): On Oct. 14, 2026, the city's chief procurement officer approved a request from the Department of Citywide Administrative Services that acknowledged the agency missed a two-day deadline to notify two low bidders that their bids were non-responsive for a contract to buy asphalt rollers, and the award went ahead to the next qualified bidder.

On October 14, 2026, pursuant to Section 1-02(h)(1)(ii) of the New York City Procurement Policy Board Rules (PPB Rules), the City Chief Procurement Officer (CCPO) ratified a Minor Rules Violation request submitted by the New York City Department of Citywide Administrative in connection with a Competitive Sealed Bid solicitation for Rollers, Asphalt DOT, EPIN 85726B0029002.

The minor rules violation occurred when the Agency failed to notify the two lowest bidders of its determination that their bids were non-responsive within the two-day period required under Section 2-07 of the PPB Rules. This oversight did not affect the evaluation of bids, compromise the integrity of the procurement process, or alter the determination to award the contract to the next lowest responsive and responsible bidder. Upon identifying the violation, the Agency notified the affected bidders and proceeded with the award in accordance with the PPB Rules.

item.description:
Probation | Special Materials | Notice In plain English (machine-written): The Department of Probation had a late public notice for a $989,807.94 extension with the Center for Alternative Sentencing and Employment Services, Inc. for its PEAK Program, which the City Chief Procurement Officer ratified on Oct. 22, 2026.

(CASES), EPIN 78125N0002001, for the provision of Pathways to Excellence, Achievement, and Knowledge (PEAK) Program services.

The contract covers the period October 1, 2024, through September 30, 2025, in the amount of $989,807.94.

The violation concerns PPB Rule § 2-11, as the required public notice and comment process was conducted after commencement of the contract term. The notice was published in the City Record on July 7, 2025, with a public hearing held on July 17, 2025.

DOP determined that the procedural violation did not have a significant adverse impact on the procurement process or its outcome. item.description:

COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG)

ALTERNATIVE ENFORCEMENT PROGRAM (AEP) 5-YEAR REVIEW - 2026

NOTICE OF INTENT TO REQUEST RELEASE OF FUNDS (NOI RROF)

             

REQUEST FOR RELEASE OF FUNDS

On or about October 8, 2026, the City of New York (the City) anticipates submitting a request to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) for the release of $51,780,000 of Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) funds authorized under the Housing and Community Development Act of 1992, to undertake the Citys Demolition Program citywide, for a period of five years.

The Alternative Enforcement Program (AEP) is intended to address the serious physical deterioration of the most distressed buildings in New York City. item.title: NOTICE OF FILING - 43-58 11TH STREET, QUEENS
item.description:
School Construction Authority | Special Materials | Notice In plain English (machine-written): The School Construction Authority has filed notice of a proposed site at 43-58 11th Street in Long Island City, Queens, for a new 972-seat intermediate school on a roughly 1.08-acre lot.

NOTICE OF FILING

Pursuant to §1731 of the New York Public Authorities Law, notice has been filed for the proposed site selection of all or portions of Block 453, Lot 1 and any other property in the immediate vicinity which may be necessary for the proposed construction of a new, approximately 972-seat intermediate school in Queens.

The proposed site is located at 43-58 11th Street on the north side of 44th Avenue, between 10th Street and 11th Street in the Long Island City neighborhood of Queens. The site is currently occupied by one to two-story commercial and manufacturing buildings. The proposed site to be acquired by the New York City School Construction Authority, on behalf of the New York City Department of Education, is an approximately 47,255 square foot (1.08 acre) lot.

item.title: NYCBenefits Concept Paper - 06926Y0443
item.description:
Dept. of Social Svcs/Human Resources Administration | Special Materials | Notice

Notice of Concept Paper

The NYC Department of Social Service (DSS)/Human Resources Administration (HRA) is committed to strengthening and modernizing the NYCBenefits Program to promote accountability, workforce capacity, cross-system coordination, and high-quality, client-centered services. The purpose of this document is to:
 

  1. Outline HRAs proposed enhancements to the NYCBenefits service model;
  2. Solicit stakeholder feedback regarding program design and operational requirements;
  3. Assess provider interest and organizational capacity; and
  4. Inform the development of a Request for Proposals (RFP)/RFx.

Anticipated number of contracts: Between thirty-eight (38) and fifty-eight (58), aligned with the following provider specializations:
 

  • Thirty-five (35) to fifty-three (53) Direct service vendors
  • Three (3) to five (5) Technical Assistance vendors


Anticipated annual funding: $9,750,0000 to $14,950,000 over the three (3) year contract term (approximately $300-$350 per client), subject to funding availability.
